Neeraj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 31 March, 2026

 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Gwalior

 (Neeraj Vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh )

entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Sanjeev Kumar Agrawal - Advocate for appellant.
Shri Mohit Shivhare - Public Prosecutor for the State.

The appellant has been convicted for the offence punishable under Section 450 Ipc and sentenced
to undergo three years' Ri with fine of Rs.500/-, under Section 376 (1) Ipc and sentenced to
undergo ten years' Ri with fine of Rs.2000/- and under Section 323 Ipc and sentenced to undergo
three months' Ri with fine of Rs.500/-, with default stipulations by the learned First Additional
Sessions Judge, Karera, Shivpuri (M.P.) in S.T.No.108/2020 vide judgment dated 18.10.2023.
I.A.No.3195/2026 has been filed by the appellant under Section 389 (1) of Cr.P.C./430 of BNSS which is second application seeking suspension of sentence.

First application (I.A.No.19423/2024)
for suspension of sentence was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 12.09.2024.
Learned counsel appearing for the appellant submits that the appellant has already spent a period of more than five years in custody.
This Court, vide order dated 17.02.2026, summoned the custody report of the appellant, which indicates that the appellant is in jail for approximately five years and two months.

Learned counsel appearing for the appellant submits that even on merits, the appellant has a good case, as the prosecutrix was 70 years of age, whereas the appellant was aged about 32 years old at the time of the 2 CRA-5882-2024 incident.
There is no likelihood of this appeal coming up for final hearing in near future; therefore, he prays that the jail sentence be suspended and bail be granted to the appellant.
On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the State oppose the criminal appeal and prays for its rejection.
Taking into consideration the aforesaid submissions, I.A.No.3195/2026 is hereby allowed.

Subject to depositing of fine amount, if not already deposited, and on furnishing a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court, the remaining jail sentence of the appellant shall remain suspended and he be released on bail.
The appellant is further directed to mark his appearance before the concerned trial Court on 23.06.2026 and on subsequent dates given by the trial Court in this regard.
